A_target.statement:
Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a [[Definition:Complete Metric Space|complete metric space]].
Let $f_1, \ldots, f_m: X \to X$ be [[Definition:Contraction Mapping|contractions]].
Then there is a [[Definition:Unique|unique]] non-empty [[Definition:Compact Space|compact]] $K \subseteq X$ such that:
:$\displaystyle K = \bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^m \map {f_i} K$

B_source.statement:
Let $\struct {Y, \rho}$ be a [[Definition:Complete Metric Space|complete metric space]] and $T: Y \to Y$ with $\map \rho {T x, T y} \le q \, \map \rho {x, y}$ for some $q < 1$.
Then $T$ has a [[Definition:Unique|unique]] [[Definition:Fixed Point|fixed point]].

substitutions.the complete metric space: the space of nonempty compact sets with the Hausdorff metric
substitutions.the contraction T: the Hutchinson operator sending a set S to the union of f_i(S)

derived.the contraction constant: the maximum of the individual contraction ratios

object_map.reformulation: The fixed point is not a point of the ambient space but a set, so the whole problem must be lifted to the hyperspace of compact sets before the contraction principle applies.

validity_conditions: each f_i must be a contraction on the ambient space, so the Hutchinson operator contracts in Hausdorff distance
the space of nonempty compact subsets must be complete under the Hausdorff metric, which holds when the ambient space is complete
the index set must be finite for the union to remain compact
proof_plan: Let $\map {\mathcal K} X$ be the set of non-empty compact subsets of $X$, with the [[Definition:Hausdorff Distance|Hausdorff distance]] $d_H$.
As $X$ is complete, so is $\struct {\map {\mathcal K} X, d_H}$.

Define the [[Definition:Hutchinson Operator|Hutchinson operator]]:
:$\displaystyle \map {\mathcal H} A = \bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^m \map {f_i} A$
Then:
:$\map {d_H} {\map {\mathcal H} A, \map {\mathcal H} B} \le \paren {\max_i q_i} \map {d_H} {A, B}$
where $q_i$ is the contraction ratio of $f_i$.
By the [[Banach Fixed-Point Theorem]], $\mathcal H$ has a unique fixed point $K \in \map {\mathcal K} X$.
